```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

col_main <- "#2c7fb8"
col_grey <- "#9aa5b1"
col_warn <- "#d95f02"

# Small tables built by scripts/10_dashboard_data.R, so this page loads fast
p2 <- readRDS("../data/processed/p2_rate_by_severity.rds")
p4 <- readRDS("../data/processed/p4_path_share.rds")
ke <- read_csv("../data/raw/kenya_urls.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

crit <- p2$by_severity |> filter(severity == "CRITICAL")
med  <- p2$by_severity |> filter(severity == "MEDIUM")
```

# What gets exploited

## Row {height=25%}

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "CVEs in CISA KEV (exploited)"
list(icon = "shield-exclamation", color = "primary",
     value = paste0(round(p2$overall$rate_pct, 2), "%"))
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Critical vs Medium: how many times more often exploited"
list(icon = "graph-up-arrow", color = "warning",
     value = paste0(round(crit$rate_pct / med$rate_pct), " times"))
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Scored CVEs analysed (published 2016 onwards)"
list(icon = "database", color = "light",
     value = scales::comma(p2$overall$n))
```

## Row {height=75%}

```{r}
#| title: "Critical CVEs are exploited about 10 times as often as Medium ones"
d <- p2$by_severity
plot_ly(d, x = ~severity, y = ~rate_pct, type = "bar",
        marker = list(color = col_main),
        text = ~paste0(round(rate_pct, 2), "%  (n = ", scales::comma(n), ")"),
        textposition = "outside", cliponaxis = FALSE,
        hovertemplate = paste0("%{x}<br>Exploited: %{y:.2f}%<br>",
                               "CVEs: ", scales::comma(d$n),
                               "<br>In KEV: ", d$n_exploited, "<extra></extra>")) |>
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "CVSS severity"),
         yaxis = list(title = "Exploited (%)", rangemode = "tozero"),
         margin = list(t = 30))
```

::: {.card title="How to read this"}
Each bar is the share of CVEs in that severity band that CISA has confirmed as
exploited in the wild (the KEV list).

Exploitation is rare: only `r round(p2$overall$rate_pct, 2)`% of scored CVEs are
in KEV. Severity helps, but it is not a strong predictor on its own.

KEV mainly lists products used by US government agencies, so this shows
**known** exploitation, not all exploitation.
:::

# Phishing

## Row {height=25%}

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Legitimate Kenyan URLs in our own list"
list(icon = "globe-africa", color = "primary",
     value = nrow(ke))
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Kenyan URLs with a path (not a bare homepage)"
list(icon = "link-45deg", color = "warning",
     value = paste0(round(p4$share_pct[p4$group == "Our Kenyan list"]), "%"))
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Dataset's legitimate URLs with a path"
list(icon = "exclamation-triangle", color = "light",
     value = paste0(round(p4$share_pct[p4$group == "Dataset: legitimate"]), "%"))
```

## Row {height=75%}

```{r}
#| title: "Most Kenyan URLs have a path, but the dataset's legitimate URLs never do"
pd <- p4 |> mutate(group = fct_reorder(group, share_pct))
plot_ly(pd, x = ~share_pct, y = ~group, type = "bar", orientation = "h",
        color = ~group,
        colors = c("Our Kenyan list" = col_main, "Dataset: phishing" = col_warn,
                   "Dataset: legitimate" = col_grey),
        text = ~paste0(round(share_pct, 1), "%  (n = ", scales::comma(n), ")"),
        textposition = "outside", cliponaxis = FALSE, showlegend = FALSE,
        hovertemplate = "%{y}<br>%{x:.1f}% have a path<extra></extra>") |>
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "URLs with a path after the domain (%)", range = c(0, 110)),
         yaxis = list(title = ""),
         margin = list(l = 10, r = 30))
```

```{r}
#| title: "Our Kenyan list mixes homepages, login pages and deeper pages"
tp <- ke |>
  count(page_type) |>
  mutate(page_type = factor(page_type,
                            levels = c("homepage", "login_service", "deep"),
                            labels = c("Homepage", "Login / service", "Deeper page")),
         share = round(100 * n / sum(n)))
plot_ly(tp, x = ~page_type, y = ~n, type = "bar", marker = list(color = col_main),
        text = ~paste0(n, "  (", share, "%)"), textposition = "outside",
        cliponaxis = FALSE,
        hovertemplate = "%{x}<br>%{y} URLs<extra></extra>") |>
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "Page type"),
         yaxis = list(title = "Number of URLs", rangemode = "tozero"),
         margin = list(t = 30))
```

::: {.card title="Why the Kenyan test matters"}
Every legitimate URL in the phishing dataset is a bare homepage. A model trained
on it may learn "has a path means phishing", which would wrongly flag real
Kenyan login and deeper pages.

The Kenyan false-alarm rate is still to come from the phishing model (Part 4).
:::
